title: Karma Yoga
summary: Shree Krishna expounds on karm yog or the yog of action. He explains that nobody can remain without action, even for a moment. Bound by their inherent modes of nature, all beings are always engaged in some work. Superior are those who practice karm yog and continue to work diligently to fulfill their responsibilities externally, but internally they are unattached to them.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन |
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ||
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Janardan, if You consider knowledge superior to action, then why do You ask me to wage this terrible war?
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca
jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
verses.meaning: arjuna uvāca - Arjuna said; jyāyasī - superior; cet - if; karmaṇaḥ - than action; te - by you; matā - considered; buddhiḥ - knowledge; janārdana - O Krishna; tat - then; kim - why; karmaṇi - in action; ghore - terrible; mām - me; niyojayasi - do you engage; keśava - O Krishna

verses.sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे |
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ||
verses.translation: My intellect is bewildered by Your ambiguous advice. Please tell me decisively the one path by which I may attain the highest good.
verses.transliteration:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me
tad ekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām
verses.meaning: vyāmiśreṇa iva - by your ambiguous; vākyena - words; buddhim - intellect; mohayasi - bewildering; iva - as it were; me - my; tad - therefore; ekam - one; vada - tell; niścitya - decisively; yena - by which; śreyaḥ - highest good; aham - I; āpnuyām - may attain

verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ |
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ||
verses.translation: The Lord said: O sinless one, the two paths leading to enlightenment were previously explained by Me: the path of knowledge, for those inclined toward contemplation, and the path of work for those inclined toward action.
verses.transliteration:
śrī-bhagavān uvāca
loke 'smin dvi-vidhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karma-yogena yoginām
verses.meaning: śrī-bhagavān uvāca - the Lord said; loke asmin - in this world; dvi-vidhā - two kinds; niṣṭhā - paths; purā - previously; proktā - explained; mayā - by Me; anagha - O sinless one; jñāna-yogena - through path of knowledge; sāṅkhyānām - for contemplatives; karma-yogena - through path of action; yoginām - for yogis

verses.sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते |
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ||
verses.translation: One cannot achieve freedom from karmic reactions by merely abstaining from work, nor can one attain perfection of knowledge by mere physical renunciation.
verses.transliteration:
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute
na ca sannyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
verses.meaning: na - not; karmaṇām - of actions; anārambhāt - by abstaining; naiṣkarmyam - freedom from karma; puruṣaḥ - a person; aśnute - attains; na - nor; ca - and; sannyasanāt - by renunciation; eva - alone; siddhim - perfection; samadhigacchati - attains

verses.sanskrit:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् |
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ||
verses.translation: There is no one who can remain without action even for a moment. Indeed, all beings are compelled to act by their qualities born of material nature (the three guṇas).
verses.transliteration:
na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarma-kṛt
kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ
verses.meaning: na hi - never; kaścit - anyone; kṣaṇam api - even a moment; jātu - ever; tiṣṭhati - remains; akarma-kṛt - without acting; kāryate - is made to act; hi - certainly; avaśaḥ - helplessly; karma - action; sarvaḥ - all; prakṛti-jaiḥ - born of nature; guṇaiḥ - by the modes

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् |
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ||
verses.translation: Those who restrain the external organs of action, while continuing to dwell on sense objects in the mind, certainly delude themselves and are to be called hypocrites.
verses.transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
verses.meaning: karma-indriyāṇi - organs of action; saṃyamya - restraining; yaḥ - who; āste - sits; manasā - in mind; smaran - remembering; indriyārthān - sense objects; vimūḍha-ātmā - deluded; mithyā-ācāraḥ - hypocrite; saḥ - they; ucyate - are called

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन |
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ||
verses.translation: But those karm yogis who control their knowledge senses with the mind, O Arjuna, and engage the working senses in working without attachment, are certainly superior.
verses.transliteration:
yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate 'rjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
verses.meaning: yaḥ - who; tu - but; indriyāṇi - senses; manasā - by mind; niyamya - controlling; ārabhate - engages; arjuna - O Arjuna; karma-indriyaiḥ - organs of action; karma-yogam - work in devotion; asaktaḥ - unattached; saḥ - they; viśiṣyate - excel

verses.sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः |
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ||
verses.translation: You should thus perform your prescribed Vedic duties, since action is superior to inaction. By ceasing activity, even your bodily maintenance will not be possible.
verses.transliteration:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ
śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
verses.meaning: niyatam - prescribed; kuru - perform; karma - duty; tvam - you; karma - action; jyāyaḥ - superior; hi - for; akarmaṇaḥ - to inaction; śarīra-yātrā - bodily maintenance; api - even; ca - and; te - your; na - not; prasiddhyet - would be possible; akarmaṇaḥ - without action

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः |
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ||
verses.translation: Work must be done as a yajña to the Supreme Lord; otherwise, work causes bondage in this material world. Therefore, O son of Kunti, for the satisfaction of God, perform your prescribed duties, without being attached to the results.
verses.transliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṃ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samācara
verses.meaning: yajña-arthāt - for sake of sacrifice; karmaṇaḥ - than work; anyatra - else; lokaḥ - world; ayam - this; karma-bandhanaḥ - bound by karma; tat-artham - for that; karma - work; kaunteya - O Arjuna; mukta-saṅgaḥ - free from attachment; samācara - perform properly

verses.sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः |
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ||
verses.translation: In the beginning of creation, Brahma created humankind along with duties, and said, "Prosper in the performance of these yajñas (sacrifices), for they shall bestow upon you all you wish to achieve."
verses.transliteration:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stviṣṭa-kāma-dhuk
verses.meaning: saha-yajñāḥ - with sacrifice; prajāḥ - humankind; sṛṣṭvā - having created; pura - in the beginning; uvāca - said; prajāpatiḥ - Brahma; anena - by this; prasaviṣyadhvam - prosper; eṣaḥ - this; vaḥ - your; astu - let be; iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk - giver of desired objects

verses.sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः |
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ||
verses.translation: By your sacrifices, the celestial gods will be pleased, and by cooperation between humans and the celestial gods, great prosperity will reign for all.
verses.transliteration:
devān bhāvayatānen te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
verses.meaning: devān - the gods; bhāvayata - please; anena - by this; te - they; devāḥ - the gods; bhāvayantu - will please; vaḥ - you; parasparam - one another; bhāvayantaḥ - pleasing; śreyaḥ - prosperity; param - supreme; avāpsyatha - you shall attain

verses.sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः |
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ||
verses.translation: The celestial gods, being satisfied by the performance of sacrifice, will grant you all the desired necessities of life. But those who enjoy what is given to them, without making offerings in return, are verily thieves.
verses.transliteration:
iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāya ebhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
verses.meaning: iṣṭān - desired; bhogān - enjoyments; hi - certainly; vaḥ - to you; devāḥ - gods; dāsyante - will give; yajña-bhāvitāḥ - pleased by sacrifice; taiḥ - by them; dattān - given; apradāya - without offering; ebhyaḥ - to them; yaḥ - who; bhuṅkte - enjoys; stenaḥ - thief; eva - verily; saḥ - they

verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः |
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ||
verses.translation: The spiritually-minded, who eat food that is first offered in sacrifice, are released from all kinds of sin. Others, who cook food for their own enjoyment, verily eat only sin.
verses.transliteration:
yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt
verses.meaning: yajña-śiṣṭa - remnants of sacrifice; aśinaḥ - eaters; santaḥ - saintly; mucyante - are freed; sarva - all; kilbiṣaiḥ - from sins; bhuñjate - eat; te - they; tu - but; agham - sin; pāpāḥ - sinners; ye - who; pacanti - cook; ātma-kāraṇāt - for own sake

verses.sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः |
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ||
verses.translation: All living beings subsist on food, and food is produced by rains. Rains come from the performance of sacrifice, and sacrifice is produced by the performance of prescribed duties.
verses.transliteration:
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ
verses.meaning: annāt - from food; bhavanti - subsist; bhūtāni - beings; parjanyāt - from rain; anna-sambhavaḥ - food is produced; yajñāt - from sacrifice; bhavati - comes; parjanyaḥ - rain; yajñaḥ - sacrifice; karma-samudbhavaḥ - produced from duty

verses.sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् |
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ||
verses.translation: The duties for human beings are described in the Vedas, and the Vedas are manifested by God Himself. Therefore, the all-pervading Lord is eternally present in acts of sacrifice.
verses.transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣara-samudbhavam
tasmāt sarva-gataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
verses.meaning: karma - action; brahma-udbhavam - from Vedas; viddhi - know; brahma - Vedas; akṣara - imperishable; samudbhavam - originating; tasmāt - therefore; sarva-gatam - all-pervading; brahma - Supreme; nityam - eternally; yajñe - in sacrifice; pratiṣṭhitam - established

verses.sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः |
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ||
verses.translation: O Parth, those who do not accept their responsibility in the cycle of sacrifice established by the Vedas are sinful. They live only for the delight of their senses; indeed their lives are in vain.
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayaty iha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
verses.meaning: evam - thus; pravartitam - set in motion; cakram - wheel; na - not; anuvartayati - follows; iha - here; yaḥ - who; agha-āyuḥ - sinful life; indriya-ārāmaḥ - delighting in senses; mogham - in vain; pārtha - O Arjuna; saḥ - they; jīvati - live

verses.sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः |
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ||
verses.translation: But those who rejoice in the self, who are illumined and fully satisfied in the self, for them, there is no duty.
verses.transliteration:
yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś ca mānavaḥ
ātmany eva ca santuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
verses.meaning: yaḥ - who; tu - but; ātma-ratiḥ - delight in self; eva - alone; syāt - is; ātma-tṛptaḥ - satisfied in self; ca - and; mānavaḥ - person; ātmani - in self; eva - only; ca - and; santuṣṭaḥ - content; tasya - for them; kāryam - duty; na - no; vidyate - exists

verses.sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन |
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ||
verses.translation: Such self-realized souls have nothing to gain or lose either in discharging or renouncing their duties. Nor do they need to depend on other living beings to fulfill their self-interest.
verses.transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana
na cāsya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ
verses.meaning: na - not; eva - indeed; tasya - for them; kṛtena - by action; arthaḥ - gain; na - nor; akṛtena - by inaction; iha - here; kaścana - any; na - nor; ca - and; asya - their; sarva-bhūteṣu - on any being; kaścit - any; artha - purpose; vyapāśrayaḥ - dependence

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर |
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ||
verses.translation: Therefore, giving up attachment, perform actions as a matter of duty because by working without being attached to the fruits, one attains the Supreme.
verses.transliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti puruṣaḥ
verses.meaning: tasmāt - therefore; asaktaḥ - unattached; satatam - always; kāryam - duty; karma - work; samācara - perform; asaktaḥ - unattached; hi - certainly; ācaran - performing; karma - work; param - Supreme; āpnoti - attains; puruṣaḥ - person

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः |
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ||
verses.translation: By performing their prescribed duties, King Janak and others attained perfection. You should also perform your duties to set an example for the good of the world.
verses.transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṃgraham evāpi sampaśyan kartum arhasi
verses.meaning: karmaṇā eva - by action alone; hi - certainly; saṃsiddhim - perfection; āsthitāḥ - attained; janaka-ādayaḥ - Janaka and others; loka-saṃgraham - welfare of world; eva api - even; sampaśyan - considering; kartum - to do; arhasi - you should

verses.sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः |
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||
verses.translation: Whatever actions great persons perform, common people follow. Whatever standards they set, all the world pursues.
verses.transliteration:
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
verses.meaning: yat yat - whatever; ācarati - does; śreṣṭhaḥ - great person; tat tat - that; eva - certainly; itaraḥ - others; janaḥ - people; saḥ - they; yat - whatever; pramāṇam - standard; kurute - set; lokaḥ - world; tat - that; anuvartate - follows

verses.sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन |
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ||
verses.translation: There is no duty for Me to do in all the three worlds, O Parth, nor do I have anything to gain or attain. Yet, I am engaged in prescribed duties.
verses.transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
verses.meaning: na - not; me - for Me; pārtha - O Arjuna; asti - is; kartavyam - duty; triṣu - in three; lokeṣu - worlds; kiñcana - any; na - nor; anavāptam - unattained; avāptavyam - to be attained; varte - I am engaged; eva - yet; ca - and; karmaṇi - in duties

verses.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः |
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ||
verses.translation: For if I did not carefully perform the prescribed duties, O Parth, all men would follow My path in all respects.
verses.transliteration:
yadi hy ahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
verses.meaning: yadi - if; hi - certainly; aham - I; na - not; varteyam - were to engage; jātu - ever; karmaṇi - in duty; atandritaḥ - diligently; mama - My; vartma - path; anuvartante - would follow; manuṣyāḥ - people; pārtha - O Arjuna; sarvaśaḥ - in all ways

verses.sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् |
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ||
verses.translation: If I ceased to perform prescribed actions, all these worlds would perish. I would be responsible for the pandemonium that would prevail, and would thereby destroy the peace of the human race.
verses.transliteration:
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṃ karma ced aham
saṅkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
verses.meaning: utsīdeyuḥ - would perish; ime - these; lokāḥ - worlds; na - not; kuryām - were I to do; karma - duty; cet - if; aham - I; saṅkarasya - of chaos; ca - and; kartā - cause; syām - would be; upahanyām - would destroy; imāḥ - these; prajāḥ - people

verses.sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत |
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ||
verses.translation: As ignorant people perform their duties with attachment to the results, O scion of Bharat, so should the wise act without attachment, for the sake of leading people on the right path.
verses.transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāṃs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur loka-saṃgraham
verses.meaning: saktāḥ - attached; karmaṇi - to work; avidvāṃsaḥ - ignorant; yathā - as; kurvanti - act; bhārata - O Arjuna; kuryāt - should do; vidvān - wise; tathā - so; asaktaḥ - unattached; cikīrṣuḥ - wishing; loka-saṃgraham - welfare of world

verses.sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् |
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ||
verses.translation: The wise should not create discord in the intellects of ignorant people, who are attached to fruitive actions, by inducing them to stop work. Rather, by performing their duties in an enlightened manner, they should inspire the ignorant also to do their prescribed duties.
verses.transliteration:
na buddhi-bhedaṃ janayed ajñānāṃ karma-saṅginām
joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
verses.meaning: na - not; buddhi-bhedam - discord in understanding; janayet - should create; ajñānām - of ignorant; karma-saṅginām - attached to work; joṣayet - should inspire; sarva-karmāṇi - all duties; vidvān - wise; yuktaḥ - united; samācaran - performing

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः |
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ||
verses.translation: All activities are carried out by the three modes of material nature. But in ignorance, the soul, deluded by false identification with the body, thinks of itself as the doer.
verses.transliteration:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ
ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
verses.meaning: prakṛteḥ - of nature; kriyamāṇāni - are performed; guṇaiḥ - by the modes; karmāṇi - actions; sarvaśaḥ - all; ahaṅkāra - ego; vimūḍha-ātmā - deluded soul; kartā - doer; aham - I; iti - thus; manyate - thinks

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः |
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इत्येव मत्वा न सज्जते ||
verses.translation: O mighty-armed Arjuna, illumined persons distinguish the soul as distinct from guṇas and karmas. They perceive that it is only the guṇas (in the shape of the senses, mind) that move among the guṇas (objects), and thus they do not get entangled.
verses.transliteration:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta ity eva matvā na sajjate
verses.meaning: tattva-vit - knower of truth; tu - but; mahā-bāho - O mighty-armed; guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ - of guṇas and karma; guṇāḥ - guṇas; guṇeṣu - among guṇas; vartante - act; iti - thus; eva - indeed; matvā - knowing; na - not; sajjate - get entangled

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु |
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ||
verses.translation: Those who are deluded by the operation of the guṇas become attached to the results of their actions. But the wise who understand these truths should not unsettle such ignorant people who know very little.
verses.transliteration:
prakṛter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsna-vin na vicālayet
verses.meaning: prakṛteḥ - of nature; guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ - deluded by guṇas; sajjante - become attached; guṇa-karmasu - to actions; tān - them; akṛtsna-vidaḥ - of imperfect knowledge; mandān - dull; kṛtsna-vit - one with full knowledge; na - not; vicālayet - should unsettle

verses.sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा |
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ||
verses.translation: Performing all works as an offering unto Me, constantly meditate on Me as the Supreme. Become free from desire and selfishness, and with your mental grief departed, fight!
verses.transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi sannyasyādhyātma-cetasā
nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ
verses.meaning: mayi - unto Me; sarvāṇi - all; karmāṇi - works; sannyasya - renouncing; adhyātma-cetasā - with mind on Supreme; nirāśīḥ - free from desire; nirmamaḥ - free from mine; bhūtvā - being; yudhyasva - fight; vigata-jvaraḥ - free from mental fever

verses.sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः |
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ||
verses.translation: Those who abide by these teachings of Mine, with profound faith and free from envy, are released from the bondage of karma.
verses.transliteration:
ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ
śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ
verses.meaning: ye - who; me - My; matam - teaching; idam - this; nityam - constantly; anutiṣṭhanti - follow; mānavāḥ - humans; śraddhāvantaḥ - with faith; anasūyantaḥ - without envy; mucyante - are freed; te - they; api - also; karmabhiḥ - from karma

verses.sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् |
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ||
verses.translation: But those who find faults with My teachings, being bereft of knowledge and devoid of discrimination, they disregard these principles and bring about their own ruin.
verses.transliteration:
ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ
verses.meaning: ye - who; tu - but; etat - this; abhyasūyantaḥ - criticizing; na - not; anutiṣṭhanti - follow; me - My; matam - teaching; sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhān - deluded in all knowledge; tān - them; viddhi - know; naṣṭān - ruined; acetasaḥ - without discrimination

verses.sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्या प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि |
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ||
verses.translation: Even wise people act according to their natures, for all living beings are propelled by their natural tendencies. What will one gain by repression?
verses.transliteration:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
verses.meaning: sadṛśam - accordingly; ceṣṭate - acts; svasyāḥ - of their own; prakṛteḥ - nature; jñānavān - wise; api - even; prakṛtim - nature; yānti - follow; bhūtāni - beings; nigrahaḥ - restraint; kim - what; kariṣyati - will do

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ |
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ||
verses.translation: The senses naturally experience attachment and aversion to the sense objects, but do not be controlled by them, for they are way-layers and foes.
verses.transliteration:
indriyasya indriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau
tayor na vaśam āgacchettau hy asya paripanthinau
verses.meaning: indriyasya - of senses; indriyasya arthe - for sense objects; rāga-dveṣau - attachment and aversion; vyavasthitau - situated; tayoḥ - of them; na - not; vaśam - under control; āgacchet - come; tau - those; hi - for; asya - his; paripanthinau - foes

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् |
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||
verses.translation: It is far better to perform one's natural prescribed duty, though tinged with faults, than to perform another's prescribed duty, though perfectly. In fact, it is preferable to die in the discharge of one's duty, than to follow the path of another, which is fraught with danger.
verses.transliteration:
śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ
verses.meaning: śreyān - better; sva-dharmaḥ - own duty; viguṇaḥ - with faults; para-dharmāt - than another's duty; sva-anuṣṭhitāt - well performed; sva-dharme - in own duty; nidhanam - death; śreyaḥ - better; para-dharmaḥ - another's duty; bhaya-āvahaḥ - causing fear

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पुरुषः |
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ||
verses.translation: Arjuna asked: Why is a person impelled to commit sinful acts, even unwillingly, as if by force, O descendant of Vrishni (Krishna)?
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca
atha kena prayukto 'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati puruṣaḥ
anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
verses.meaning: arjuna uvāca - Arjuna said; atha - then; kena - by what; prayuktaḥ - impelled; ayam - this; pāpam - sin; carati - commits; puruṣaḥ - person; anicchan - unwilling; api - even; vārṣṇeya - O Krishna; balāt - by force; iva - as if; niyojitaḥ - compelled

verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः |
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: It is lust alone, which is born of contact with the mode of passion, and later transformed into anger. Know this as the sinful, all-devouring enemy in the world.
verses.transliteration:
śrī-bhagavān uvāca
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam
verses.meaning: śrī-bhagavān uvāca - the Lord said; kāmaḥ - lust; eṣaḥ - this; krodhaḥ - anger; eṣaḥ - this; rajaḥ-guṇa - mode of passion; samudbhavaḥ - born of; mahā-aśanaḥ - all-devouring; mahā-pāpmā - great sin; viddhi - know; enam - this; iha - in world; vairiṇam - enemy

verses.sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च |
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ||
verses.translation: Just as a fire is covered by smoke, a mirror is masked by dust, and an embryo is concealed by the womb, similarly one's knowledge gets shrouded by desire.
verses.transliteration:
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena ca
yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam
verses.meaning: dhūmena - by smoke; āvriyate - is covered; vahniḥ - fire; yathā - as; ādarśaḥ - mirror; malena - by dust; ca - and; yathā - as; ulbena - by womb; āvṛtaḥ - covered; garbhaḥ - embryo; tathā - so; tena - by that; idam - this; āvṛtam - is covered

verses.sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा |
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ||
verses.translation: The knowledge of even the most discerning gets covered by this perpetual enemy in the form of insatiable desire, which is never satisfied and burns like fire, O son of Kunti.
verses.transliteration:
āvṛtaṃ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
verses.meaning: āvṛtam - covered; jñānam - knowledge; etena - by this; jñāninaḥ - of the wise; nitya-vairiṇā - perpetual enemy; kāma-rūpeṇa - in form of desire; kaunteya - O Arjuna; duṣpūreṇa - insatiable; analena - like fire; ca - and

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते |
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ||
verses.translation: The senses, mind, and intellect are said to be breeding grounds of desire. Through them, it clouds one's knowledge and deludes the embodied soul.
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate
etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam
verses.meaning: indriyāṇi - senses; manaḥ - mind; buddhiḥ - intellect; asya - its; adhiṣṭhānam - seat; ucyate - are said; etaiḥ - by these; vimohayati - deludes; eṣaḥ - this; jñānam - knowledge; āvṛtya - covering; dehinam - embodied soul

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ |
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ||
verses.translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, in the very beginning bring the senses under control and slay this enemy called desire, which is the embodiment of sin and destroys knowledge and realization.
verses.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hy enaṃ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam
verses.meaning: tasmāt - therefore; tvam - you; indriyāṇi - senses; ādau - first; niyamya - controlling; bharata-ṛṣabha - O best of Bharatas; pāpmānam - sinful; prajahi - slay; hi - certainly; enam - this; jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam - destroyer of knowledge

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः |
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ||
verses.translation: The senses are superior to the gross body, and superior to the senses is the mind. Beyond the mind is the intellect, and even beyond the intellect is the soul.
verses.transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ
verses.meaning: indriyāṇi - senses; parāṇi - superior; āhuḥ - they say; indriyebhyaḥ - to senses; param - superior; manaḥ - mind; manasaḥ - to mind; tu - but; parā - superior; buddhiḥ - intellect; yaḥ - who; buddheḥ - to intellect; parataḥ - beyond; tu - but; saḥ - that (soul)

verses.sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना |
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ||
verses.translation: Thus knowing the soul to be superior to the material intellect, O mighty armed Arjuna, subdue the lower self (senses, mind, and intellect) by the higher self (strength of the soul), and kill this formidable enemy called lust.
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā
jahi śatruṃ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṃ durāsadam
verses.meaning: evam - thus; buddheḥ - than intellect; param - superior; buddhvā - knowing; saṃstabhya - subduing; ātmānam - the self; ātmanā - by the self; jahi - slay; śatrum - enemy; mahā-bāho - O mighty-armed; kāma-rūpam - in form of desire; durāsadam - hard to overcome
